outcome: Help authorised teams discover, reuse and license archive content with source, rights, restrictions and provenance visible.
overview: Regional broadcasters, publishers and cultural archives hold decades of Arabic and international material, yet thin metadata and rights records scattered across contracts leave most of it unfindable and unsellable. This solution indexes video, audio and images by what is actually in them — speech, faces, objects and on-screen text — and joins that index to the authoritative rights record, so every result arrives with its source, territory, window and restrictions visible. Collections, clearance requests and licensing briefs run through an approval workflow with a usage audit trail. An 8–12 week pilot on one bounded collection targets faster discovery and clearance, with librarians and the rights desk retaining approval authority.

benefits.text: Cut the time to find and clear an archive asset by a target 40%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target from the source catalogue, to validate against the customer’s own discovery and clearance baseline during the pilot — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Grow the approved reuse and licensing pipeline by making the catalogue searchable by content rather than by file name
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on digitisation coverage, index quality and existing licensing demand; revenue is realised only through the customer’s own sales process

benefits.text: Keep restricted and expired-rights material out of search results and exports through hard rights filters
benefits.source: Architecture design — rights and permission filters run before results are returned, not as ranking signals
benefits.limits: Only as reliable as the authoritative rights register; assets with unresolved rights are quarantined rather than silently allowed

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); archive essence, derived indexes and rights records remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: There is no authoritative rights record for the collection in scope
notFor.why: Search results are only safe to act on when a rights source of truth can answer territory, window and talent questions; similarity between assets never establishes ownership

notFor.situation: The collection is largely un-digitised tape, film or paper
notFor.why: Indexing operates on digital essence and proxies; holdings that exist only on physical carriers cannot be searched by any of this

notFor.situation: Automated licensing without human clearance is the goal
notFor.why: Clearance carries contractual and legal consequence and stays with the rights team by design; the system shortlists, it does not licence

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns cataloguing standards, the rights register and every clearance decision · Duration: 8–12 week pilot; further 16–28 weeks to enterprise rollout
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, media-indexing engineer, search engineer; customer archive owner, rights owner, commercial licensing lead, security approver · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and baseline agreement
2) Repository, rights-register and access-model integration
3) Extraction and index build with relevance benchmarking
4) Clearance workflow build and librarian UAT
5) Training and controlled rollout on the pilot collection
6) Stabilisation and handover

Metadata quality thresholds met on the pilot collection
Licensing export reconciles to the rights register and librarian UAT is complete
